Here’s a shorter, divorce-centered rewrite that leans into starting over, reinventing yourself, and finding God in the dark:  

---

No one chooses heartbreak or divorce, but those seasons have a way of shaping us in ways nothing else can. They strip you down and force you to decide who you’re going to be when the pieces no longer fit the old life.  

I’ve walked through loss, rebuilding, and the pain of starting over. It’s messy. It’s lonely. And yet, it’s also where I’ve found God most clearly — in the silence, in the tears, in the nights I didn’t know how to keep going.  

What I’ve learned is this: the fall isn’t final unless you choose to stay down. Reinvention is born in the very places you thought would destroy you. Just like a muscle grows stronger only after it’s been broken down, our faith and character grow when we’re willing to rise again.  

“Though the righteous fall seven times, they rise again.” — Proverbs 24:16  

So if you’re in the dark right now, don’t quit. Don’t let divorce, failure, or pain define you. Let it refine you. Build a circle of people who lift you, and cling to the God who never leaves you.  

He is good, even here. And He will meet you right where you are.  

---

Do you want me to make this more **raw and personal** (like you’re talking straight from your journal) or more **polished and public-facing** (like for a Facebook/LinkedIn post)?

Here are a few types of photos that would pair beautifully with that post, given the themes of **starting over, reinvention, and finding God in dark places**:  

### 1. Symbolic Nature Imagery  
- A sunrise breaking through clouds (hope and new beginnings)  
- A path or trail disappearing into the trees (the unknown journey ahead)  
- Blooming flowers or green growth emerging from cracked soil (renewal after struggle)  

### 2. Personal but Subtle Imagery  
- A candid photo of you walking forward, from behind (movement into a new chapter)  
- Your silhouette against a sunset or wide-open landscape (reflection and resilience)  
- A simple black-and-white portrait that feels raw and grounded (vulnerability and strength)  

### 3. Faith-Centered Imagery  
- Light streaming through stained glass or trees (God’s presence in darkness)  
- Hands open toward the sky (surrender and faith)  
- A cross or simple symbol of faith blended into a natural setting  

### 4. Minimalist / Metaphorical  
- A single candle glowing in the dark (hope in the darkness)  
- Footprints in the sand (a journey, one step at a time)  
- An open door with light spilling through (transition and new beginnings)  

✨ My recommendation: if you want it **more personal**, go with a silhouette or walking-forward photo of yourself. If you want it **more symbolic**, choose sunrise or light-breaking-through-darkness imagery.

Here’s a rewritten version that feels like **your** voice — authentic, resilient, faith-centered, and tied to the arc of your life and work:  

---

Nobody sets out hoping for hard seasons. Yet somehow, they’re often the chapters we remember most — not because of the pain they bring, but because of the faith, grit, and character they pull out of us.  

I’m no stranger to hard times. My struggles aren’t special — they’re simply mine. Just like yours are yours. We all carry battles that at times feel too heavy to lift. Right now, I’m in another one of those seasons. Truthfully? I don’t like it. I’m not thrilled about being here…again. It can feel like every time you find your footing, life sweeps your legs out and sends you straight back into the mud. But here I am. Maybe you’re here too. And if you are, maybe this will speak to you.  

Here’s what I’ve learned: the only true shame isn’t in being knocked down — it’s in choosing to stay there. Whether it’s finances, relationships, faith, business, or anything else, the fall is never final unless you decide it is.  

Think about the gym: you tear muscle down so it can rebuild stronger. Life is no different. Struggle is the soil where strength grows. Before you can build what’s solid, the weak parts have to go.  

I’ve come to believe these seasons are a gift. A hard gift, yes, but a gift nonetheless — one that proves just how resilient you really are… if you’re willing to keep getting back up.  

“For though the righteous fall seven times, they rise again…” — Proverbs 24:16  

So if you’re in the thick of it right now, keep getting up. Don’t quit. Don’t let the mud define you. Let the scars become proof of what you’ve survived and who you’re becoming.  

I’m deeply grateful for God’s faithfulness and for the circle of family and friends who lift me when I can’t lift myself. If you don’t have that circle yet, build it. We were never meant to fight these battles alone — and learning that has been one of my hardest but most life-giving lessons.  

God is still good. Even when times aren’t. And He will always meet you right where you are.  

---
